title: Forschungszentrum Jülich and ARQUE Systems Secure €35 Million ($38.4 Million USD) to Build 200-Qubit Silicon Spin Quantum Computer - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Forschungszentrum Jülich and its spin-off ARQUE Systems launched Q-STAR.NRW, a €35 million ($38.4 million) project running through end-2029 to build a silicon spin quantum computer with up to 200 qubits for deployment in JUNIQ at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre. Funding is 90% German federal money under the Coal Regions Investment Act and 10% from North Rhine-Westphalia, and ARQUE's patented electron-shuttling architecture targets long-term scaling beyond ten million qubits on a 2x2 cm die.

insights.claim: Forschungszentrum Jülich and its spin-off ARQUE Systems have launched Q-STAR.NRW, a €35 million ($38.4 million USD) initiative running through the end of 2029 to develop and integrate a semiconductor-based quantum computer with up to 200 qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Sets a 2029 milestone of 200 qubits for a European silicon spin effort; track delivery against this timeline as a benchmark for the spin-qubit modality.
insights.locator: Forschungszentrum Jülich and its Jülich–Aachen spin-off

insights.claim: The €35 million Q-STAR.NRW quantum computer project is financed 90% through German federal funds under the Coal Regions Investment Act and 10% by the State of North Rhine-Westphalia via Forschungszentrum Jülich, tying quantum hardware funding to coal-region structural transition money.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shows German public money for quantum is flowing through regional-development channels, not only dedicated quantum programs; a funding source to watch for other European quantum startups.
insights.quote: Financed 90% through German federal funds under the Coal Regions Investment Act
insights.locator: Forschungszentrum Jülich and its Jülich–Aachen spin-off

insights.claim: The 200-qubit Q-STAR.NRW system will be deployed into the Jülich UNified Infrastructure for Quantum Computing (JUNIQ) at the Jülich Supercomputing Centre, building on ARQUE Systems' earlier integration of a five-qubit prototype into JUNIQ.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Jump from a five-qubit prototype to 200 qubits is a 40x scale-up; ARQUE's ability to execute it is the key watch item.
insights.locator: Building on ARQUE Systems’ prior integration

insights.claim: ARQUE Systems' processor encodes quantum information in the spins of individual electrons trapped in silicon and silicon-germanium structures, and its patented shuttling architecture moves electrons across the chip to shared interaction and control zones instead of using fixed nearest-neighbor couplings and dedicated control lines for every qubit.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Shared control zones are ARQUE's patented differentiator versus per-qubit wiring designs; IP position matters if the approach proves out.
insights.quote: transports electrons across the chip to shared interaction and control zones, reducing wiring overhead
insights.locator: Building on ARQUE Systems’ prior integration

insights.claim: Because electron shuttling reduces wiring overhead, ARQUE Systems targets long-term scaling of its silicon spin architecture beyond ten million qubits on a two-by-two-centimeter die.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: An aspirational long-term target, far from the 200-qubit 2029 goal; treat it as a roadmap claim, not near-term capability.
insights.quote: targeting long-term scaling beyond ten million qubits on a two-by-two-centimeter die
insights.locator: Building on ARQUE Systems’ prior integration

insights.claim: Q-STAR.NRW partners will develop hybrid quantum-HPC software stacks, algorithms, and user-support services to connect the 200-qubit processor with the Jülich Supercomputing Centre's classical supercomputers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Adds to the trend of embedding quantum processors inside HPC centers; relevant to vendors of quantum-HPC integration software.

insights.claim: The Q-STAR.NRW infrastructure is meant to give academic researchers and small and medium-sized enterprises in the Rhenish mining region access to test applications in materials development, chemistry, pharmaceuticals, and logistics.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Target use cases are the usual early-quantum candidates; adoption by regional SMEs is a soft demand signal, not commercial revenue.

insights.claim: The Jülich Supercomputing Centre has previously deployed NVIDIA DGX Quantum together with Quantum Machines and ARQUE Systems, according to earlier Quantum Computing Report coverage.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Links ARQUE to NVIDIA's quantum-classical integration ecosystem; one more data point on NVIDIA's reach into quantum control.
